From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Decision anchors & acceptance workstream for pilot (MAP draft)

Helena —

Thanks again for a productive kickoff yesterday. Attached is a compact mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the evaluation workstream and the specific acceptance criteria we discussed. High-level items below so the procurement and technical teams can align quickly: 

1) Success signals (what "good" looks like) — proposed anchors:
   - Latency: median inference < 250ms for 512-token requests (95th < 450ms)
   - Quality: task-level F1 / accuracy targets per dataset (see matrix)
   - Reliability: sustained 99.5% availability during validation window
   - Cost guardrail: projected inference cost per 10k requests <= $X (TBD after sizing)

2) Exit gates (hard stop conditions):
   - Data leakage or PII handling gaps not remediated in 5 business days
   - Sustained error rate > 3% for more than one day during smoke/validation
   - Unresolved compliance questions flagged by Acme security team

3) Acceptance tests we plan to run during validation:
   - Smoke: 100 canned queries covering main intents (pass/fail binary)
   - Throughput: 1k concurrent requests for 30 minutes to verify autoscaling behavior
   - Regression: compare model outputs against golden set and measure deltas
   - Adversarial prompts: defined list to check hallucination and PII suppression

I've included the MAP workbook (decision_anchors_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a compact acceptance_test_matrix.csv. Please review thresholds in the sheet and mark any changes inline — I can update and circulate a version for signatures.

Proposed timeline (sampling):
   - Week 0: MAP sign-off & access provisioning
   - Week 1: Integration + smoke tests
   - Week 2: Validation window (metrics collection & exec review)
   - Week 3: Final acceptance and cutover plan

Would you be able to review by EOD Friday so procurement can start their review next week? If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our solutions/devs to walk through the acceptance tests in detail.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Team —

Adding a technical note for the acceptance test runbook so we have no ambiguity during validation: 

- Eval harness: we'll run the harness in a shadow mode against Acme staging for 48 hours. The harness will produce per-test metrics (latency distribution, token usage, top-5 label accuracy). Instructions uploaded (eval_harness_instructions.md).
- Golden set: Acme to provide up to 250 labeled examples for the core intents. We will lock the golden set before regression runs.
- Failure classification: any mismatch where F1 drops > 5 points or hallucination rate increases by > 4% will be marked as a blocking defect and routed to a joint triage.
- Rollback trigger: if more than 2 blocking defects are found during a single validation day, we will pause the validation and execute the rollback checklist in the MAP (owner: Redwood SRE + Acme Eng).

Also: recommend we include one post-validation executive checkpoint where we review metrics and agree on a production ramp schedule.

Questions for Karthik: do we want to include a short smoke checklist for data access provisioning (S3 read permissions, KMS key access, IP allowlist) as a pre-condition in the MAP?

– Priyom
